detailed_rationale:
AXISCADES Technologies is an engineering-services provider focused on Aerospace, Defence, and ESAI (Electronics, Semiconductors, and AI) domains, a segment benefiting from a real, identifiable policy tailwind -- India's defence-indigenization and 'Make in India' defence-manufacturing push, alongside global aerospace OEMs outsourcing engineering work to India. FY26 revenue grew a healthy 12% to Rs.1,159 Cr, continuing a genuinely good longer-run track record (5-year sales CAGR 17%, 5-year profit CAGR 21.4%). The company is also investing in capacity, having completed a ~Rs.39.4 Cr land acquisition in Telangana in July 2026, consistent with a defence-manufacturing capacity build-out.

The key earnings-quality issue is Q4 FY26: revenue of Rs.273 Cr but net profit of only Rs.0.42 Cr, driven by an unusually high 96% effective tax rate that quarter -- a clear one-off distorting the full-year reported profit (Rs.72 Cr) downward, since the other three quarters of FY26 each posted a healthy Rs.21-28 Cr profit. Normalizing Q4 to a more typical quarterly run-rate (say, in line with Q1-Q3) would put full-year profit closer to Rs.95-100 Cr rather than the reported Rs.72 Cr, which would bring the effective P/E down from the headline 84.6x to roughly 60-65x -- still a full valuation, but less alarming than the reported multiple suggests. ROE (~11%) and ROCE (~15.3%) are decent but not exceptional for that even-normalized multiple.

Reverse-DCF: even giving credit for the Q4 tax-rate normalization, a ~60-65x effective multiple for an ~11% ROE, 12%-revenue-growth engineering-services business is still a stretch -- the sector tailwind (defence indigenization) is real, but the price already assumes a good deal of it plays out, and we do not think the normalization argument is enough to call this cheap, only less expensive than the headline number implies.
recommendation_rationale: We are keeping the quant Sell. While we believe the reported 84.6x P/E overstates the true richness of the stock (Q4 FY26's 96% tax rate was very likely a one-off dragging full-year profit down), even a normalized ~60-65x multiple is not attractively priced for an ~11% ROE business, notwithstanding the genuine and real defence-indigenization tailwind. We flag the normalization point explicitly so the headline multiple is not taken entirely at face value, but it does not change the underlying Sell call.
summary: AXISCADES Technologies provides engineering services to the aerospace and defence sectors, a segment with a genuine tailwind from India's defence-indigenization push, and has grown revenue 12% in FY26 with a good 5-year track record (17% revenue CAGR, 21% profit CAGR). However, an unusually high tax charge in the most recent quarter dragged reported full-year profit down, making the headline ~85 times earnings look more extreme than the underlying run-rate suggests; even normalized, we estimate the effective multiple is still a full ~60-65 times earnings against an approximately 11% return on equity. We rate this a Sell on valuation.
positive_para: A real, structural policy tailwind from India's defence-indigenization and 'Make in India' manufacturing push, a genuinely good longer-run track record (17% revenue and 21% profit CAGR over 5 years), continued capacity investment (Telangana land acquisition, July 2026), and 12% revenue growth in FY26 despite the reported profit weakness.
negative_para: An unusually high 96% effective tax rate in Q4 FY26 (versus healthy profit in the prior three quarters) distorted the full-year reported profit downward to just Rs.72 Cr -- even normalizing for this one-off, the effective valuation remains a full ~60-65 times earnings against an approximately 11% return on equity, which does not leave much room for execution missteps in a still-developing defence-engineering order book.
reverse_dcf_judgment: The reported 84.6x P/E is inflated by a one-off Q4 tax charge; normalizing to a ~60-65x effective multiple against an ~11% ROE is still a full price for the demonstrated (as opposed to hoped-for) profitability, even with a genuine defence-sector tailwind behind it.
